due to \" - Abort message\n269\t    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General compilation errors\n270\t\n271\t    for line in stderr.lines() {\n272\t        let line = line.trim();\n273\t\n274\t        // Check for Rust compiler error codes (e.g., \"error[E0308]:\")\n275\t        if line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n276\t            compilation_failed = true;\n277\t            if let Some(msg) = parse_error_line(line) {\n278\t                error_messages.push(msg);\n279\t            }\n280\t            continue;\n281\t        }\n282\t\n283\t        // Check for \"could not compile\" message\n284\t        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n285\t            compilation_failed = true;\n286\t            if let Some(crate_name) = extract_crate_name(line) {\n287\t                error_messages.push(format!(\"Failed to compile crate: {}\", crate_name));\n288\t            } else {\n289\t                error_messages.push(\"Compilation failed\".to_string());\n290\t            }\n291\t            continue;\n292\t        }\n293\t\n294\t        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n295\t        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n296\t        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n297\t            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n298\t                error_messages.push(format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count));\n299\t            }\n300\t            continue;\n301\t        }\n302\t\n303\t        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n304\t        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n305\t            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n306\t            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n307\t                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n308\t                compilation_failed = true;\n309\t                error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n310\t            }\n311\t        }\n312\t    }\n313\t\n314\t    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n315\t}\n316\t\n317\t/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n318\t///\n319\t/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n320\t/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\n321\tfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n322\t    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n323\t    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n324\t        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n325\t            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n326\t            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n327\t            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n328\t            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n329\t                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n330\t            }\n331\t        }\n332\t    }\n333\t    None\n334\t}\n335\t\n336\t/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n337\t///\n338\t/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n339\t/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\n340\tfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n341\t    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n342\t        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n343\t            if start < end {\n344\t                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n345\t            }\n346\t        }\n347\t    }\n348\t    None\n349\t}\n350\t\n351\t/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n352\t///\n353\t/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n354\t/// Output: Some(3)\n355\tfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n356\t    // Find the number in the line\n357\t    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n358\t    for word in words {\n359\t        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n360\t            return Some(n);\n361\t        }\n362\t    }\n363\t    None\n364\t}\n365\t\n366\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n367\t// Cargo Test Runner\n368\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n369\t\n370\t/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n371\t///\n372\t/// ## Example\n373\t///\n374\t/// ```no_run\n375\t/// use needle::cargo_test::{CargoTest, TestArgs};\n376\t/// use std::path::Path;\n377\t///\n378\t/// let args = TestArgs::new()\n379\t///     .with_target(\"--lib\")\n380\t/// CargoTest {\n386\t    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n387\t    workspace: PathBuf,\n388\t    /// Test arguments.\n389\t    args: TestArgs,\n390\t    /// Timeout in seconds.\n391\t {\n398\t            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n399\t            args: TestArgs::default(),\n400\t            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n401\t        }\n402\t    }\n403\t\n404\t    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n405\t    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n406\t        CargoTest {\n407\t            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n408\t            args,\n409\t            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n410\t        }\n411\t    }\n412\t\n413\t    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n414\t    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n415\t        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n416\t        self\n417\t    }\n418\t\n419\t    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n420\t    ///\n421\t    /// ## Errors\n422\t    ///\n423\t    /// Returns an error if:\n424\t    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n425\t    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n426\t    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n427\t    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n428\t        let start = Instant::now();\n429\t        let args = self.args.build_args();\n430\t\n431\t        tracing::info!(\n432\t            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n433\t            args = ?args,\n434\t            \"running cargo test\"\n435\t        );\n436\t\n437\t        // Build the cargo command\n438\t        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n439\t        cmd.args(&args);\n440\t        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n441\t        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n442\t        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n443\t\n444\t        // Spawn the process\n445\t        let mut child = cmd.spawn().context(\"failed to spawn cargo test\")?;\n446\t\n447\t        // Wait for completion with timeout\n448\t        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n449\t        let _exit_status = loop {\n450\t            match child.try_wait() {\n451\t                Ok(Some(status)) => break status,\n452\t                Ok(None) => {\n453\t                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n454\t                        child\n455\t                            .kill()\n456\t                            .context(\"failed to kill cargo test after timeout\")?;\n457\t                        return Ok(TestOutcome {\n458\t                            exit_code: None,\n459\t                            stdout: String::new(),\n460\t                            stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n461\t                            duration: start.elapsed(),\n462\t                            timed_out: true,\n463\t                            compilation_failed: false,\n464\t                            compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n465\t                        });\n466\t                    }\n467\t                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n468\t                }\n469\t                Err(e) => {\n470\t                    return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to wait for cargo test: {}\", e));\n471\t                }\n472\t            }\n473\t        };\n474\t\n475\t        // Capture output\n476\t        let output = child\n477\t            .wait_with_output()\n478\t            .context(\"failed to capture cargo test output\")?;\n479\t\n480\t        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n481\t        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n482\t\n483\t        // Detect compilation errors\n484\t        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n485\t            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n486\t\n487\t        tracing::info!(\n488\t            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n489\t            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n490\t            success = output.status.success(),\n491\t            compilation_failed,\n492\t            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n493\t            \"cargo test completed\"\n494\t        );\n495\t\n496\t        Ok(TestOutcome {\n497\t            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n498\t            stdout,\n499\t            stderr,\n500\t            duration: start.elapsed(),\n501\t            timed_out: false,\n502\t            compilation_failed,\n503\t            compilation_errors,\n504\t        })\n505\t    }\n506\t\n507\t    /// Get the workspace directory.\n508\t    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n509\t seconds.\n518\t    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n519\t        self.timeout_secs\n520\t    }\n521\t\n522\t    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n523\t    ///\n524\t    /// This Arguments\n528\t    ///\n529\t    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n530\t    ///\n531\t    /// ## Errors\n532\t    ///\n533\t    /// Returns an error ```no_run\n541\t    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n542\t    /// use std::path::Path;\n543\t    ///\n544\t    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n545\t    /// let test to get the outcome\n549\t        let outcome = self.run()?;\n550\t\n551\t        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n552\t        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n553\t            // Write stdout\n554\t            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n555\t                tracing::warn!(\n556\t                    test_name = %e,\n567\t                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n568\t                );\n569\t            }\n570\t\n571\t            // Write combined output\n572\t            let combined = Functions\n601\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n602\t\n603\t/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\n604\tfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n605\t    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n606\t        s.to_string()\n607\t    } else {\n608\t        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n609\t        format!(\"{}... else {\n589\t            tracing::warn!(\n590\t                test_name = %test_name,\n591\t                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n592\t            );\n593\t        }\n594\t\n595\t        Ok(outcome)\n596\t    }\n597\t}\n598\t\n599\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n600\t// Utility Functions\n601\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n602\t\n603\t/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\n604\tfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n605\t    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n606\t        s.to_string()\n607\t    } else {\n608\t        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n609\t        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n610\t    }\n611\t}\n612\t\n613\t/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n614\t///\n615\t/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n616\t///\n617\t/// ## Example\n618\t///\n619\t/// ```\n620\t/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n621\t///\n622\t/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n623\t/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n624\t/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n625\t/// ```\n626\tpub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n627\t    let mut combined = String::new();\n628\t\n629\t    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n630\t        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n631\t        combined.push_str(stdout);\n632\t        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n633\t            combined.push('\\n');\n634\t        }\n635\t    }\n636\t\n637\t    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n638\t        if !combined.is_empty() {\n639\t            combined.push('\\n');\n640\t        }\n641\t        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n642\t        combined.push_str(stderr);\n643\t        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n644\t            combined.push('\\n');\n645\t        }\n646\t    }\n647\t\n648\t    combined\n649\t}\n650\t\n651\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n652\t// compilation_failed is true\n/// if stderr contains compilation error patterns, and error_messages is a list\n/// of parsed error messages.\npub fn detect_compilation_errors(stderr: &str) -> (bool, Vec<String>) {\n    let mut compilation_failed = false;\n    let mut error_messages = Vec::new();\n\n    // Cargo compilation error patterns\n    // 1. \"error[E####]: \" - Rust compiler errors with error codes\n    // 2. \"error: could not compile \" - Compilation failed message\n    // 3. \"error: aborting due to \" - Abort message\n    // 4. \"error: \" followed by a filename - General line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            if let Some(msg) = parse_error_line(line) {\n                error_messages.push(msg);\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"could not compile\" message\n        if line.contains(\"could not compile\") {\n            compilation_failed = true;\n            if let Some(crate_name) = extract_crate_name(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Failed to compile crate: {}\", crate_name));\n            } else {\n                error_messages.push(\"Compilation failed\".to_string());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for \"aborting due to\" message\n        // Only count this if we've already seen actual compilation errors\n        if line.contains(\"aborting due to\") && compilation_failed {\n            if let Some(count) = extract_error_count(line) {\n                error_messages.push(format!(\"Aborted due to {} error(s)\", count));\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        // Check for general \"error:\" messages (but not warnings)\n        if line.starts_with(\"error:\") && !line.starts_with(\"error[E\") {\n            // Only capture if it looks like a compilation error, not a test error\n            if line.contains(\"unused\") || line.contains(\"dead_code\") || line.contains(\"mutability\") {\n                // These are compiler warnings/lints, not test failures\n                compilation_failed = true;\n                error_messages.push(line.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    (compilation_failed, error_messages)\n}\n\n/// Parse an error line to extract the error message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error[E0308]: mismatched types\"\n/// Output: Some(\"E0308: mismatched types\")\nfn parse_error_line(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Extract everything after \"error[\" until end of line\n    if let Some(start) = line.find(\"error[\") {\n        if let Some(end) = line.find(']') {\n            let error_code = &line[start + 6..end]; // Skip \"error[\"\n            let message = line[end + 1..].trim(); // Skip \"]\"\n            // Check if message is empty or just a colon\n            if !message.is_empty() && message != \":\" {\n                return Some(format!(\"{}: {}\", error_code, message));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract crate name from \"could not compile\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"error: could not compile `my_crate`\"\n/// Output: Some(\"my_crate\")\nfn extract_crate_name(line: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    if let Some(start) = line.find('`') {\n        if let Some(end) = line.rfind('`') {\n            if start < end {\n                return Some(line[start + 1..end].to_string());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n/// Extract error count from \"aborting due to\" message.\n///\n/// Input: \"aborting due to 3 previous errors\"\n/// Output: Some(3)\nfn extract_error_count(line: &str) -> Option<usize> {\n    // Find the number in the line\n    let words: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();\n    for word in words {\n        if let Ok(n) = word.parse::<usize>() {\n            return Some(n);\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo Test Runner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runner for cargo test commands.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::cargo_test::{CargoTest, TestArgs};\n/// use std::path::Path;\n///\n/// let args = TestArgs::new()\n///     .with_target(\"--lib\")\n///     .with_filter(\"integration\");\n///\n/// let runner = CargoTest::with_args(Path::new(\"/workspace\"), args);\n/// let outcome = runner.run().unwrap();\n/// ```\npub struct CargoTest {\n    /// Workspace directory where cargo will run.\n    workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Test arguments.\n    args: TestArgs,\n    /// Timeout in seconds.\n    timeout_secs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CargoTest {\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with default arguments.\n    pub fn new(workspace: &Path) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args: TestArgs::default(),\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new cargo test runner with custom arguments.\n    pub fn with_args(workspace: &Path, args: TestArgs) -> Self {\n        CargoTest {\n            workspace: workspace.to_path_buf(),\n            args,\n            timeout_secs: DEFAULT_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set a custom timeout (default is 600 seconds).\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout_secs: u64) -> Self {\n        self.timeout_secs = timeout_secs;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test with the configured arguments.\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The cargo binary cannot be found\n    /// - The workspace directory is invalid\n    /// - The process cannot be spawned\n    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let args = self.args.build_args();\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            workspace = %self.workspace.display(),\n            args = ?args,\n            \"running cargo test\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the cargo command\n        let mut cmd = Command::new(\"cargo\");\n        cmd.args(&args);\n        cmd.current_dir(&self.workspace);\n        cmd.stdout(Stdio::piped());\n        cmd.stderr(Stdio::piped());\n\n        // Spawn the process\n        let mut child = cmd.spawn().context(\"failed to spawn cargo test\")?;\n\n        // Wait for completion with timeout\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.timeout_secs);\n        let _exit_status = loop {\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(status)) => break status,\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                        child\n                            .kill()\n                            .context(\"failed to kill cargo test after timeout\")?;\n                        return Ok(TestOutcome {\n                            exit_code: None,\n                            stdout: String::new(),\n                            stderr: String::from(\"command timed out\"),\n                            duration: start.elapsed(),\n                            timed_out: true,\n                            compilation_failed: false,\n                            compilation_errors: Vec::new(),\n                        });\n                    }\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to wait for cargo test: {}\", e));\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Capture output\n        let output = child\n            .wait_with_output()\n            .context(\"failed to capture cargo test output\")?;\n\n        let stdout = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout));\n        let stderr = truncate_output(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        // Detect compilation errors\n        let (compilation_failed, compilation_errors) =\n            detect_compilation_errors(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            exit_code = ?output.status.code(),\n            duration_secs = start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            success = output.status.success(),\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_error_count = compilation_errors.len(),\n            \"cargo test completed\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(TestOutcome {\n            exit_code: output.status.code(),\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration: start.elapsed(),\n            timed_out: false,\n            compilation_failed,\n            compilation_errors,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the workspace directory.\n    pub fn workspace(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.workspace\n    }\n\n    /// Get the test arguments.\n    pub fn args(&self) -> &TestArgs {\n        &self.args\n    }\n\n    /// Get the timeout in seconds.\n    pub fn timeout_secs(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.timeout_secs\n    }\n\n    /// Run cargo test and write output to files.\n    ///\n    /// This method runs `cargo test` and writes the captured stdout, stderr,\n    /// and combined output to separate files in the `.test_outputs/<test_name>/` directory.\n    ///\n    /// ## Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `test_name` - A unique identifier for the test (e.g., \"integration_test_1\")\n    ///\n    /// ## Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - The test run fails\n    /// - Output directory creation fails\n    /// - File writing fails\n    ///\n    /// ## Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::cargo_test::CargoTest;\n    /// use std::path::Path;\n    ///\n    /// let runner = CargoTest::new(Path::new(\"/workspace\"));\n    /// let outcome = runner.run_with_output_files(\"my_test\").unwrap();\n    /// ```\n    pub fn run_with_output_files(&self, test_name: &str) -> Result<TestOutcome> {\n        // First run the test to get the outcome\n        let outcome = self.run()?;\n\n        // Create test output directory and write outputs\n        if let Some(output) = TestOutput::new(test_name, &self.workspace) {\n            // Write stdout\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stdout(&outcome.stdout) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stdout to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write stderr\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_stderr(&outcome.stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write stderr to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            // Write combined output\n            let combined = create_combined_output(&outcome.stdout, &outcome.stderr);\n            if let Err(e) = output.write_combined(&combined) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    test_name = %test_name,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to write combined output to file\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            tracing::info!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                stdout_path = %output.stdout_path().display(),\n                stderr_path = %output.stderr_path().display(),\n                combined_path = %output.combined_path().display(),\n                \"test output written to files\"\n            );\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                test_name = %test_name,\n                \"failed to create test output directory, output files not written\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(outcome)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Utility Functions\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Truncate output to at most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.\nfn truncate_output(s: &str) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES {\n        s.to_string()\n    } else {\n        let truncated = &s[..MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES];\n        format!(\"{}... [truncated]\", truncated)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create combined output from stdout and stderr.\n///\n/// This function combines stdout and stderr into a single string with section headers.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::cargo_test::create_combined_output;\n///\n/// let stdout = \"Test output line 1\\nTest output line 2\";\n/// let stderr = \"Error message\";\n/// let combined = create_combined_output(stdout, stderr);\n/// ```\npub fn create_combined_output(stdout: &str, stderr: &str) -> String {\n    let mut combined = String::new();\n\n    if !stdout.is_empty() {\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDOUT ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stdout);\n        if !stdout.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !stderr.is_empty() {\n        if !combined.is_empty() {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n        combined.push_str(\"=== STDERR ===\\n\");\n        combined.push_str(stderr);\n        if !stderr.ends_with('\\n') {\n            combined.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n\n    combined\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n182\t\n183\t/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n184\t///\n185\t/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n186\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n187\tpub enum Outcome {\n188\t    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n189\t    Success,\n190\t    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n191\t    Failure,\n192\t    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n193\t    Timeout,\n194\t    /// Exit 126 code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n199\t    Crash(i32),\n200\t}\n201\t\n202\timpl Outcome {\n203\t    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n204\t    ///\n205\t    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n206\t    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n207\t    ///\n208\t    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n209\t    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n210\t    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n211\t    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n212\t    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n213\t    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n214\t    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n215\t    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n216\t    /// - all other → `Failure`\n217\t    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n218\t        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n219\t        if was_interrupted {\n220\t            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n221\t        }\n222\t\n223\t        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n224\t        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n225\t        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n226\t        match exit_code {\n227\t            // Success\n228\t            0 => Outcome::Success,\n229\t            // Explicit failure code\n230\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n231\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n232\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n233\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n234\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n235\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n236\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n237\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n238\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n239\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n240\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n241\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n242\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n243\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n244\t        }\n245\t    }\n246\t\n247\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n248\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n249\t        match self {\n250\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n251\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n252\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n253\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n254\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n255\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n256\t        }\n257\t    }\n258\t}\n259\t\n260\t// };\n1055\t        let _: &dyn std::error::Error = &e;\n1056\t    }\n1057\t}\n1058\t\n1059\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1060\t// IdleAction\n1061\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1062\t\n1063\t/// What a worker does when the queue is empty.\n1064\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]\n1065\t#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\n1066\tpub enum IdleAction {\n1067\t    /// Poll again after `idle_timeout` seconds.\n1068\t    #[default]\n1069\t    Wait,\n1070\t    /// Exit cleanly.\n1071\t    Exit,\n1072\t}\n1073\t\n1074\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1075\t// BeadAction\n1076\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1077\t\n1078\t/// Action taken on a bead by the outcome handler.\n1079\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n1080\tpub enum BeadAction {\n1081\t    /// Bead was released back to open status.\n1082\t    Released,\n1083\t    /// Bead was deferred (e.g., timeout with deferred label).\n1084\t BeadStatus {\n120\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n121\t        match self {\n122\t            BeadStatus::Open => write!(f, \"open\"),\n123\t            BeadStatus::InProgress => write!(f, \"in_progress\"),\n124\t            BeadStatus::Done | BeadStatus::Closed => write!(f, \"done\"),\n125\t            BeadStatus::Blocked => write!(f,    WorkerState::Claiming => \"CLAIMING\",\n165\t            WorkerState::Retrying => \"RETRYING\",\n166\t            WorkerState::Building => \"BUILDING\",\n167\t            WorkerState::Dispatching ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n182\t\n183\t/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n184\t///\n185\t/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n186\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n187\tpub enum Outcome {\n188\t    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n189\t    Success,\n190\t    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n191\t    Failure,\n192\t    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n193\t    Timeout,\n194\t    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n195\t    AgentNotFound,\n196\t    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n197\t    Interrupted,\n198\t    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n199\t    Crash(i32),\n200\t}\n201\t\n202\timpl Outcome {\n203\t    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n204\t    ///\n205\t    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n206\t    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n207\t    ///\n208\t    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n209\t    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n210\t    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n211\t    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n212\t    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n213\t    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n214\t    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n215\t    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n216\t    /// - all other → `Failure`\n217\t    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n218\t        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n219\t        if was_interrupted {\n220\t            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n221\t        }\n222\t\n223\t        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n224\t        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n225\t        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n226\t        match exit_code {\n227\t            // Success\n228\t            0 => Outcome::Success,\n229\t            // Explicit failure code\n230\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n231\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n232\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n233\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n234\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n235\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n236\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n237\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n238\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n239\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n240\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n241\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n242\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n243\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n244\t        }\n245\t    }\n246\t\n247\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n248\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n249\t        match self {\n250\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n251\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n252\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n253\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n254\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n255\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n256\t        }\n257\t    }\n258\t}\n259\t\n260\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n261\t// StrandError / StrandResult\n262\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n263\t\n264\t/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n265\t#[derive(Debug)]\n266\tpub enum StrandError {\n267\t    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n268\t    ConfigError(String),\n269\t}\n270\t\n271\timpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n272\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n273\t        match self {\n274\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e),\n275\t            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n276\t        }\n277\t    }\n278\t}\n279\t\n280\timpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n281\t    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n282\t        match self {\n283\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n284\t            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n285\t        }\n286\t    }\n287\t}\n288\t\n289\t/// Result of a strand BeadStatus::Closed => write!(f, \"done\"),\n            BeadStatus::Blocked => write!(f, \"blocked\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// WorkerState\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Worker finite-state-machine states.\n///\n/// Every state has defined entry conditions, actions, and exit transitions.\n/// There are no implicit states or fallthrough paths.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE\")]\npub enum WorkerState {\n    Booting,\n    Selecting,\n    Claiming,\n    Retrying,\n    Building,\n    Dispatching,\n    Executing,\n    Handling,\n    Logging,\n    /// All strands returned empty — worker has nothing to do.\n    Exhausted,\n    /// Received graceful shutdown signal.\n    Stopped,\n    /// Unrecoverable error.\n    Errored,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for WorkerState {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        let s = match self {\n            WorkerState::Booting => \"BOOTING\",\n            WorkerState::Selecting => \"SELECTING\",\n            WorkerState::Claiming => \"CLAIMING\",\n            WorkerState::Retrying => \"RETRYING\",\n            WorkerState::Building => \"BUILDING\",\n            WorkerState::Dispatching => \"DISPATCHING\",\n            WorkerState::Executing => \"EXECUTING\",\n            WorkerState::Handling => \"HANDLING\",\n            WorkerState::Logging => \"LOGGING\",\n            WorkerState::Exhausted => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            WorkerState::Stopped => \"STOPPED\",\n            WorkerState::Errored => \"ERRORED\",\n        };\n        f.write_str(s)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Outcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n///\n/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Outcome {\n    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n    Failure,\n    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n    Timeout,\n    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n    AgentNotFound,\n    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n    Interrupted,\n    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n    Crash(i32),\n}\n\nimpl Outcome {\n    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n    ///\n    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n    ///\n    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - all other → `Failure`\n    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n        if was_interrupted {\n            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n        }\n\n        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n            // Failure range: 2-123\n            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate outcome after exhausting all candidates for a selection cycle.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    /// Successfully claimed a bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an error.\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BrDependency\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br` JSON output.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct BrDependency {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n    pub status: String,\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A bead as returned from the bead store.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Bead {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Stored as `description` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"description\")]\n    pub body: Option<String>,\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    pub status: BeadStatus,\n    /// br emits `\"\"` for unassigned beads; normalize to `None`.\n    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = \"empty_string_as_none\")]\n    pub assignee: Option<String>,\n    /// br may omit this field when empty.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Stored as `source_repo` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"source_repo\", default)]\n    pub workspace: std::path::PathBuf,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependencies: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependents: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    // br ready --json omits updated_at; default to now so explore can deserialize it\n    #[serde(default = \"chrono::Utc::now\")]\n    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Raw output from an agent process (before outcome classification).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n//      /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// IdleAction\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// What a worker does when the queue is empty.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum IdleAction {\n    /// Poll again after ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Action taken on a bead by the outcome handler.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum BeadAction {\n    /// Bead was released back to open status.\n    Released,\n    /// Bead was deferred (e.g., timeout with deferred label).\n    Deferred,\n    /// An alert bead was created.\n    Alerted,\n    /// No action taken (e.g., success with bead already closed).\n    None,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for BeadAction {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            BeadAction::Released => write!(f, \"released\"),\n            BeadAction::Deferred => write!(f, \"deferred\"),\n            BeadAction::Alerted => write!(f, \"alerted\"),\n            BeadAction::None => write!(f, \"none\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HandlerResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of handling an agent outcome.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct HandlerResult {\n    /// The classified outcome.\n    pub outcome: Outcome,\n    /// Action taken on the bead.\n    pub bead_action: BeadAction,\n    /// Telemetry events emitted during handling.\n    pub telemetry_events: Vec<crate::telemetry::EventKind>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// IdentifierScheme\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How workers generate their unique names.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum IdentifierScheme {\n    /// Use the hostname plus a short random suffix.\n    #[default]\n    HostnameRandom,\n    /// Use a sequential integer suffix.\n    Sequential,\n    /// Use a UUID v4.\n    Uuid,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ExhaustionDiagnosis\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Diagnosis from the Knot strand when all work-finding strategies are exhausted.\n///\n/// This three-state model prevents false-positive starvation alerts by\n/// distinguishing between \"queue genuinely empty\" vs \"all work claimed by\n/// other workers\" vs \"beads exist but are invisible due to configuration.\"\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ExhaustionDiagnosis {\n    /// No beads exist in the workspace at all — queue is genuinely empty.\n    /// This is normal idle, not an alert condition.\n    NoBeadsExist,\n    /// All beads are claimed by other workers — wait for them to finish.\n    /// This is normal congestion, not an alert condition.\n    AllClaimed,\n    /// Open beads exist but Pluck found none — indicates a config error.\n    /// This is an alert condition: beads may be invisible due to label filters.\n    Invisible,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ExhaustionDiagnosis {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ExhaustionDiagnosis::NoBeadsExist => write!(f, \"no_beads_exist\"),\n            ExhaustionDiagnosis::AllClaimed => write!(f, \"all_claimed\"),\n            ExhaustionDiagnosis::Invisible => write!(f, \"invisible\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Cargo test output capture\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Captured output from a cargo test execution.\n///\n/// This struct contains the complete output from running `cargo test`,\n/// including stdout, stderr, exit code, and duration. It is designed to be\n/// serializable for storage and transmission.\n///\n/// ## Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::types::OutputCapture;\n/// use std::time::Duration;\n///\n/// let capture = OutputCapture {\n///     stdout: \"running 1 test\\ntest test_foo ... ok\".to_string(),\n///     stderr: String::new(),\n///     exit_code: Some(0),\n///     duration: Duration::from_millis(1500),\n/// };\n///\n/// assert!(capture.success());\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct OutputCapture {\n    /// Captured stdout from the test execution.\n    pub stdout: String,\n    /// Captured stderr from the test execution.\n    pub stderr: String,\n    /// Exit code from the test process. `None` if killed by signal.\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Duration of the test execution.\n    #[serde(with = \"serde_duration\")]\n    pub duration: Duration,\n}\n\nimpl OutputCapture {\n    /// Returns true if the test exited with code 0.\n    pub fn success(&self) -> bool {\n        self.exit_code == Some(0)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if the test failed (non-zero exit code).\n    pub fn failed(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.success()\n    }\n\n    /// Get the duration as milliseconds.\n    pub fn duration_ms(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.duration.as_millis() as u64\n    }\n\n    /// Get the total length of stdout and stderr in bytes.\n    pub fn total_output_len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.stdout.len() + self.stderr.len()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Serde serialization module for Duration.\n///\n/// Duration is serialized as milliseconds (u64) for JSON compatibility.\nmod serde_duration {\n    use std::time::Duration;\n\n    use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};\n\n    pub fn serialize<S>(duration: &Duration, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>\n    where\n        S: Serializer,\n    {\n        let millis = duration.as_millis() as u64;\n        millis.serialize(serializer)\n    }\n\n    pub fn deserialize<'de, D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Duration, D::Error>\n    where\n        D: Deserializer<'de>,\n    {\n        let millis = u64::deserialize(deserializer)?;\n        Ok(Duration::from_millis(millis))\n    }\n}\n\n/// A single compilation error detected from cargo test output.\n///\n/// Represents a Rust compiler error with code, message, and optional file location.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum CompilationError {\n    /// A Rust compiler error with error code (e.g., E0308).\n    RustError {\n        /// The error code (e.g., \"E0308\").\n        code: String,\n        /// The error message.\n        message: String,\n        /// Optional file path where the error occurred.\n        file: Option<String>,\n        /// Optional line number where the error occurred.\n        line: Option<usize>,\n        /// Optional column number where the error occurred.\n        column: Option<usize>,\n    },\n    /// General compilation failure without specific error code.\n    General {\n        /// Description of the failure.\n        message: String,\n    },\n    /// Abort message indicating the number of errors.\n    Abort {\n        /// Number of errors that caused the abort.\n        error_count: usize,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl CompilationError {\n    /// Returns a human-readable description of the error.\n    pub fn description(&self) -> String {\n        match self {\n            CompilationError::RustError { code, message, .. } => {\n                format!(\"{}: {}\", code, message)\n            }\n            CompilationError::General { message } => message.clone(),\n            CompilationError::Abort { error_count } => {\n                format!(\"aborting due to {} previous error(s)\", error_count)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the error code if this is a Rust compiler error.\n    pub fn error_code(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            CompilationError::RustError { code, .. } => Some(code),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this error has a file location.\n    pub fn has_location(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, CompilationError::RustError { file: Some(_), .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Get the file location as \"file:line:column\" if available.\n    pub fn location_string(&self) -> Option<String> {\n        match self {\n            CompilationError::RustError {\n                file,\n                line,\n                column,\n                ..\n            } => {\n                if let Some(f) = file {\n                    let mut loc = f.clone();\n                    if let Some(l) struct BrDependency {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n    pub status: String,\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A bead as returned from the bead store.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Bead {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Stored as `description` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"description\")]\n    pub body: Option<String>,\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    pub status: BeadStatus,\n    /// br emits `\"\"` for unassigned beads; normalize to `None`.\n    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = \"empty_string_as_none\")]\n    pub assignee: Option<String>,\n    /// br may omit this field when empty.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Stored as `source_repo` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"source_repo\", default)]\n    pub workspace: std::path::PathBuf,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependencies: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependents: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    // br ready --json omits updated_at; default to now so explore can deserialize it\n    #[serde(default = \"chrono::Utc::now\")]\n    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Raw output from an agent process (before outcome classification).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// InputMethod\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How the prompt is passed to the agent binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"method\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum InputMethod {\n    /// Write the prompt to the agent's stdin.\n    Stdin,\n    /// Write the prompt to a temp file and pass the path.\n    File {\n        /// Template for the temp file path. `{bead_id}` is substituted.\n        path_template: String,\n    },\n    /// Pass the prompt as a CLI argument.\n    Args {\n        /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Path reference to a worker's heartbeat file on disk.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HeartbeatFile {\n    pub path: std::path::PathBuf,\n}\n\n/// Health status of a peer worker as inferred from its heartbeat file.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum PeerStatus {\n    /// Heartbeat is fresh — peer is considered alive.\n    Alive {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        current_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat TTL has elapsed — peer may be stuck.\n    Stale {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        claimed_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat file is missing — peer is dead or never started.\n    Dead { heartbeat_file: HeartbeatFile },\n}\n\n// status: BeadStatus,\n    /// br emits `\"\"` for unassigned beads; normalize to `None`.\n    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = \"empty_string_as_none\")]\n    pub assignee: Option<String>,\n    /// br may omit this field when empty.\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Stored as `source_repo` in br JSON output.\n    #[serde(rename = \"source_repo\", default)]\n    pub workspace: std::path::PathBuf,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependencies: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub dependents: Vec<BrDependency>,\n    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    // br ready --json omits updated_at; default to now so explore can deserialize it\n    #[serde(default = \"chrono::Utc::now\")]\n    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Raw output from an agent process (before outcome classification).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// InputMethod\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How the prompt is passed to the agent binary.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(tag = \"method\", rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum InputMethod {\n    /// Write the prompt to the agent's stdin.\n    Stdin,\n    /// Write the prompt to a temp file and pass the path.\n    File {\n        /// Template for the temp file path. `{bead_id}` is substituted.\n        path_template: String,\n    },\n    /// Pass the prompt as a CLI argument.\n    Args {\n        /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Path reference to a worker's heartbeat file on disk.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct HeartbeatFile {\n    pub path: std::path::PathBuf,\n}\n\n/// Health status of a peer worker as inferred from its heartbeat file.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum PeerStatus {\n    /// Heartbeat is fresh — peer is considered alive.\n    Alive {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        current_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat TTL has elapsed — peer may be stuck.\n    Stale {\n        last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,\n        claimed_bead: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Heartbeat file is missing — peer is dead or never started.\n    Dead { heartbeat_file: HeartbeatFile },\n}\n\n//
